judge_assessment.explanation: I solved and back-substituted all 12 systems and every claim holds: (3,6); (3,-1); (4,3); (16,5); (3,4); tickets (7 adult, 5 child) from x+y=12 and 8x+5y=81; the fractional pair (7/5, 11/5); (5,2); problem 9 collapses to -6 = 1, so no solution; problem 10 collapses to 8 = 8, an infinite family with (2,2) as a member; the rectangle gives width 6 m and length 17 m from y = 2x+5 and 2x+2y = 46; and the mixture gives 8 L of 20% with 4 L of 50%, which does satisfy 0.2(8)+0.5(4) = 3.6. Both study-guide try-its are right too. The judge's claim that special cases are handled without treating disappearing variables as an error is supported by the artifacts in a stronger way than it states: verify.py itself flagged problem 10 MANUAL with 'listed solution(s) valid but the system has a parametric/infinite family - verify completeness by hand', the build exited 2, and final_response.md reports that honestly instead of claiming twelve clean machine checks. Problem 9's 'no solution' is verified as an empty solution set rather than asserted. I found one presentation defect the judge did not mention, but it does not touch the ACCEPT.

strengths_to_preserve: The two special cases are opposite in kind and both are handled honestly: problem 9's inconsistent system is machine-verified as an empty solution set (expected []), while problem 10's dependent system is declared MANUAL by verify.py because an infinite family cannot be counted - and the representative pair (2,2) the sheet asks for is machine-checked against both equations. This is the correct division of labour between the verifier and the human and should not be regressed into a false green.

Problem 10's stem does the pedagogical work the verifier cannot: 'If the variables disappear here too, decide what this statement means, then give one specific pair that solves the system', so the item asks for both the interpretation and a checkable value rather than only one.

The word models define their variables and units in the stem before any algebra (x adult tickets and y child tickets; x width and y length in metres; x litres of 20% and y litres of 50%), and problem 12 hands the student the acid-balance equation so the modelling step under test is the second equation, not both at once.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers renders an empty expected list as the em-dash it reserves for manual-only ids, so 'no solution' - a definite, machine-verified answer - is displayed as if there were no answer to show.
evidence: verify.json id 9 is a system entry with "expected": [], which verify.py verifies as an inconsistent system.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py render_entry: an empty joined string falls back to '---', the same glyph used for manual-only ids.

improvements.title: 'No solution' prints as an em-dash in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: In render_entry, distinguish 'the id has no expected value' (manual-only, keep '---') from 'the expected value is an empty solution set' (render 'no solution'). Apply the same treatment to relational expected values so a verified '<' or '>' prints as its symbol rather than a dash.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/test_render_quick_answers.py with two cases: a compare entry of order "relation" with expected ">", and a system entry with expected [] (no solution). Assert the rendered bank lines read "$>$" and "no solution" rather than "---". Both assertions fail against the current _fmt/render_entry and pass after the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: On a sheet where the special cases are the point of the lesson, the at-a-glance column stops blanking the answer to the no-solution item; every sheet with an inconsistent system or a comparison benefits.
improvements.risk: Very low; the change is additive and fixture-locked.

case_summary: A strong procedural-fluency ramp on substitution with no mathematical defect: I re-solved and back-substituted all twelve systems, including the fractional pair (7/5, 11/5), both special cases and all three word models, and both study-guide try-its. Its best feature is the honest handling of the special cases - problem 9's empty solution set is verified rather than asserted, and problem 10's dependent system is flagged MANUAL by verify.py itself, with the build exiting 2 and the delivery message saying so, while the representative pair (2,2) is machine-checked. The only fix worth making is cosmetic: the Quick Answers bank renders problem 9's verified 'no solution' as '---', the same glyph it uses for manual-only items, because an empty expected list falls through render_entry's fallback.
